aiUsageIntro: We are committed to responsible AI usage and transparency in all our business practices. Heard uses AI to help moderate content and surface insights from community conversations. This page shows our real-time API usage — tokens consumed by day and by endpoint — so you can see exactly how we're using these tools.
aiUsageChartSubtitle: Total tokens consumed per day, broken down by endpoint.
aiUsageFooter: Data updates in real time. Tracking began June 2026.

orgsSlide1Title: Heard is a platform for conversational voting surveys
orgsSlide1Body: Instead of static surveys, Heard lets a community vote, add their own responses, and watch a living conversation emerge in real time.
orgsStep1Desc: You create a survey with a topic and a handful of seed statements to get the conversation started.
orgsStep2Desc: Participants swipe to agree or disagree with each statement.
orgsStep3Desc: Participants can add their own statements for others to vote on, and watch results update in real time.
orgsSlide3Heading: Why Heard is better than traditional surveys
orgsSlide3Body: Heard makes collecting feedback easier, faster, and more engaging for everyone involved.
orgsBullet3aRest: — just seed the conversation with a topic and a few starter statements, then let participants add their own responses
orgsBullet3bRest: — people feel ownership over the conversation and come back to see how their statements are performing
orgsBullet3cRest: — there's already an engaged pool of people on the platform ready to participate
orgsSlide4Body: Tools like these have already been used by governments and civic bodies to gather input from millions of people.
orgsBullet4aRest: — used by the Taiwanese government to crowdsource policy on ride-sharing and other issues, with millions of participants
orgsBullet4bRest: — large-scale participatory platforms used across Latin America and Europe to engage citizens in policy-making processes
orgsBullet4cRest: — a domestic US example of a local government using this approach to meaningfully engage residents in community decisions
orgsSlide5Body: Heard is more than just a tool, it's a commitment to strengthening democratic engagement and civic participation.
orgsBullet5aRest: — legally structured to prioritize public benefit alongside profit
orgsBullet5bRest: — working toward transparency and community ownership
orgsBullet5cRest: — built to amplify voices and foster productive dialogue
orgsBullet5dRest: — with a background in civic tech and impact-focused startups
orgsSlide6Body: We are running pilot programs for organizations to see how Heard can work for your community. Share your email and we'll reach out to learn more about your needs.
orgsSlide7Heading: Thanks for signing up for the pilot program!
orgsSlide7Body: We'll reach out soon to get you started. In the meantime, feel free to explore Heard and see what the community is talking about.
